plate_findings.evidence: Hematoxylin-eosin staining of punch biopsy taken from left medial shin showing a subepidermal blister

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Panel A shows a patient biopsy with H&E evidence of a subepidermal blister, consistent with the article's diagnosis of pseudoporphyria. B: Panel B shows a patient biopsy with H&E evidence of a subepidermal blister and caterpillar bodies, supporting pseudoporphyria.
panels.attribution_text: Clark et al. Olaparib-induced pseudoporphyria in a patient with ovarian cancer.. JAAD case reports 2023. doi:10.1016/j.jdcr.2023.07.011. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: Hematoxylin-eosin staining of punch biopsy taken from left medial shin (10× magnification) showing a subepidermal blister. A, The cavity contains mononuclear cells and granulocytes—mainly neutrophils but also eosinophils. B, The blister roof comprises epidermis showing degenerative features and there are “caterpillar bodies” adherent to the undersurface of the epidermis (arrow). (A and B, Hematoxylin-eosin stain; original magnification: 10×.)
in_text_mentions: Results of the punch biopsy (Fig 2A, B) were consistent with a subepidermal bullous disorder, showing a subepidermal blister with sparse mononuclear cells and granulocytes, in addition to “caterpillar bodies” adherent to the undersurface of the epidermis. DIF test findings were positive for homogenous deposition of IgG and IgA in thick-walled blood vessels (Fig 3A, B), all of which suggested a diagnosis of PCT vs pseudoporphyria.Fig 2Hematoxylin-eosin staining of punch biopsy taken from left medial shin (10× magnification) showing a subepidermal blister. panels.rationale: Single clinical photograph showing an erythematous vesicle on the left medial shin, with the article specifically describing olaparib-induced pseudoporphyria. The lesion is marked with pen circles; skin is visibly light. Age and ethnicity are not stated in the provided caption/in-text.

in_text_mentions: erythematous macules and firm papules present on the nose, right ankle, right dorsal aspect of the foot, and bilateral lower extremities. One erythematous vesicle was present on the left medial shin (Fig 1). Psoriatic plaques, consistent with her preexisting diagnosis of psoriasis, were also present on the bilateral lower extremities. Two 4-mm punch biopsies were taken from the medial left shin, including a perilesional punch biopsy that was sent for direct immunofluorescence (DIF) testing.
